email-message.storm:
/*
Example Stix 2.1 "email-message" object:
{
    "type": "email-message",
    "spec_version": "2.1",
    "id": "email-message--0c57a304-cf87-4d60-b7c8-a68f927b9e8b",
    "is_multipart": false,
    "date": "2004-04-19T12:22:23.000Z",
    "from_ref": "email-addr--9a1f0a6e-de26-5578-93b1-3d4e6d8c1234",
    "to_refs": ["email-addr--d1b3fdb1-6b21-5da2-9dcf-89ecc98cca1f"],
    "subject": "Did you see this?",
    "body": "Check out this attachment, I think it is a picture of the aliens!"
}

Mapped to inet:email:message. NOTE: from_ref/to_refs/cc_refs/bcc_refs point
at other Stix objects (email-addr). Per-object storm callbacks only receive
$object + $bundle and have no access to nodes already built for other Stix
objects (no nodesbyid), so those refs are intentionally left unresolved here
- same limitation documented in file.storm for parent_directory_ref.

TODO - Do we want our stix tol to post-process nodes like this to resolve internal object references?
*/
[ inet:email:message=(stix, email-message, $object.id)
    :subject?=$object.subject
    :date?=$object.date
    :body?=$object.body
]
[ <(refs)+ { it:sec:stix:bundle:id=$bundle.id } ]
$node.data.set(`stix:object:bundle:{$bundle.id}`, $object)
return($node)

grouping.storm:
/*
Example Stix 2.1 "grouping" object:
{
    "type": "grouping",
    "spec_version": "2.1",
    "id": "grouping--84e4d88f-44ea-4bcd-bbf3-b2c1c320bcb3",
    "created": "2020-01-16T20:28:23.000Z",
    "modified": "2020-01-16T20:28:23.000Z",
    "name": "Malware Campaign Grouping",
    "description": "A grouping of objects related to a single malware campaign.",
    "context": "malware-analysis",
    "object_refs": [
        "malware--16d2358f-a3e1-4fca-b839-e33566a069b5",
        "indicator--c410e480-e42b-47d1-9476-85307c12bcda"
    ]
}

Mapped to meta:note, matching the existing note.storm/opinion.storm pattern
for generic container/narrative Stix objects. object_refs do NOT need manual
handling - the Stix ingest engine (LibStixImport.ingest) automatically adds
"refs" edges for the literal "object_refs" field after all objects are built.
*/
[ meta:note=(stix, grouping, $object.id)
    :type=`stix.grouping.{$object.context}`
    :text?=$object.description
    :created?=$object.created
    :updated?=$object.modified
]
[ <(refs)+ { it:sec:stix:bundle:id=$bundle.id } ]
$node.data.set(`stix:object:bundle:{$bundle.id}`, $object)
return($node)

incident.storm:
/*
Example Stix 2.1 "incident" object (core Incident SDO is intentionally
minimal in Stix 2.1 - richer detail is added via the Incident Core Extension):
{
    "type": "incident",
    "spec_version": "2.1",
    "id": "incident--f6cec2e5-4e9d-49b1-b7b8-9ba38c5f6a54",
    "created": "2023-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
    "modified": "2023-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
    "name": "Ransomware Compromise of Acme Corp",
    "description": "Acme Corp was compromised via a phishing email that led to a ransomware deployment."
}

Mapped to risk:compromise with its name and description. Incident extension
fields are preserved in node data.
*/
[ risk:compromise=(stix, incident, $object.id)
    :name?=$object.name
    :desc?=$object.description
]
[ <(refs)+ { it:sec:stix:bundle:id=$bundle.id } ]
$node.data.set(`stix:object:bundle:{$bundle.id}`, $object)
return($node)

location.storm:
/*
Example Stix 2.1 "location" object (real sample, trimmed, from
tests/data/cisa_stix_bun.json):
{
    "type": "location",
    "spec_version": "2.1",
    "id": "location--34610caa-9135-4875-ac37-4746088dd006",
    "created": "2024-02-02T15:11:50.25412Z",
    "modified": "2024-02-02T15:11:50.25412Z",
    "name": "203.95.8.98",
    "description": "Domain Name: pdsguam.biz\r\nRegistrar: GoDaddy.com, LLC ... (truncated whois text)",
    "region": "northern-america",
    "country": "US"
}

Mapped to geo:place, which mirrors the reverse (export) mapping already used
by synapse.lib.stormlib.stix for geo:place <-> location. That reverse mapping
reads :loc/:latlong, so this sets the same props from the Stix side.
*/
[ geo:place=(stix, location, $object.id)
    :name?=$object.name
    :desc?=$object.description
]
if ($object.country != $lib.null) {
    [ :loc?=$object.country.lower() ]
}
if (($object.latitude != $lib.null) and ($object.longitude != $lib.null)) {
    [ :latlong?=($object.latitude, $object.longitude) ]
}
[ <(refs)+ { it:sec:stix:bundle:id=$bundle.id } ]
$node.data.set(`stix:object:bundle:{$bundle.id}`, $object)
return($node)

observed-data.storm:
/*
Example Stix 2.1 "observed-data" object:
{
    "type": "observed-data",
    "spec_version": "2.1",
    "id": "observed-data--b67d30ff-02ac-498a-92f9-32f845f448cf",
    "created": "2016-04-06T19:58:16.000Z",
    "modified": "2016-04-06T19:58:16.000Z",
    "first_observed": "2016-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "last_observed": "2016-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "number_observed": 1,
    "object_refs": [
        "ipv4-addr--efcd5e80-570c-4107-b6fb-963f78038002"
    ]
}

Mapped to meta:note (same fallback used for note.storm/opinion.storm/
grouping.storm), since Synapse has no single form matching this generic
"observation event" concept. number_observed is preserved via the raw Stix
object stashed in nodedata below. object_refs are auto-linked as refs edges
by the Stix ingest engine itself - no manual handling needed here.
*/
[ meta:note=(stix, observed-data, $object.id)
    :type=stix.observed-data
    .seen?=$object.first_observed
    .seen?=$object.last_observed
]
[ <(refs)+ { it:sec:stix:bundle:id=$bundle.id } ]
$node.data.set(`stix:object:bundle:{$bundle.id}`, $object)
return($node)

process.storm:
/*
Example Stix 2.1 "process" object:
{
    "type": "process",
    "spec_version": "2.1",
    "id": "process--f7a5c7bb-8c4a-4d55-9c39-7cf6e4e5c1c8",
    "pid": 1221,
    "created_time": "2016-01-20T14:11:25.55Z",
    "cwd": "/tmp",
    "command_line": "./gedit-bin --new-window",
    "binary_ref": "file--3128d3ac-6b0e-4f1b-8f6c-cee29d9a6b78"
}

Mapped to it:exec:proc. Working directory and process-specific references
are preserved in node data rather than conflated with the executable path.
*/
[ it:exec:proc=(stix, process, $object.id)
    :pid?=$object.pid
    :time?=$object.created_time
    :cmd?=$object.command_line
]
[ <(refs)+ { it:sec:stix:bundle:id=$bundle.id } ]
$node.data.set(`stix:object:bundle:{$bundle.id}`, $object)
return($node)

sighting.storm:
/*
Example Stix 2.1 "sighting" object:
{
    "type": "sighting",
    "spec_version": "2.1",
    "id": "sighting--ee20065d-2555-424f-ad9e-0f8428623c75",
    "created": "2016-04-06T20:08:31.000Z",
    "modified": "2016-04-06T20:08:31.000Z",
    "first_seen": "2015-12-21T19:00:00.000Z",
    "last_seen": "2015-12-21T19:00:00.000Z",
    "count": 1,
    "sighting_of_ref": "indicator--26ffb872-1dd9-446e-b6f5-d58527e5b5d2",
    "observed_data_refs": [
        "observed-data--b67d30ff-02ac-498a-92f9-32f845f448cf"
    ]
}

IMPORTANT: unlike "relationship" objects, "sighting" objects are NOT diverted
before reaching config['objects'] in Synapse's LibStixImport.ingest (only the
literal type "relationship" is special-cased) - this file genuinely executes
for every Stix "sighting" object. sighting_of_ref and observed_data_refs point
at other Stix objects and cannot be resolved here (no nodesbyid access at
this stage) - same limitation as elsewhere in this folder. Mapped to
meta:note as a fallback since Synapse has no dedicated "sighting" form.
*/
[ meta:note=(stix, sighting, $object.id)
    :type=stix.sighting
    .seen?=$object.first_seen
    .seen?=$object.last_seen
]
[ <(refs)+ { it:sec:stix:bundle:id=$bundle.id } ]
$node.data.set(`stix:object:bundle:{$bundle.id}`, $object)
return($node)

threat-actor.storm:
/*
Resolved: yes, this mirrors the exact mapping Vertex uses in their own
default Stix ingest config (synapse.lib.stormlib.stix.stixingest) for
threat-actor -> ps:contact, so this is the intentional/confirmed choice.
*/
[ ps:contact=(stix, threat-actor, $object.id)
    :name?=$object.name
    :desc?=$object.description
    :names?=$object.aliases
]
[ <(refs)+ { it:sec:stix:bundle:id=$bundle.id } ]
$node.data.set(`stix:object:bundle:{$bundle.id}`, $object)
return($node)
